pr.title: Retry webhook deliveries with exponential backoff
pr.author: dana
pr.body:
Webhook deliveries fail permanently on any transient error today. This adds retries with full-jitter backoff and tracks delivery status.

- [x] retry helper
- [x] status enum
- [ ] migration (follow-up)

summary.tldr: Webhook sends now **retry up to 5 times** with jittered exponential backoff, and deliveries record a `status` and `attempts` count instead of a `delivered` boolean.
summary.why: Deliveries currently fail permanently on the first transient error (timeouts, 5xx). Customers miss events and support has to redeliver by hand.
summary.how:
1. `DeliveryStatus` enum replaces the boolean in `app/models/webhook.py`.
2. A generic `with_retry()` helper in `app/delivery/retry.py`.
3. `send()` wraps the POST in `with_retry()` and records the outcome.
4. The redeliver API returns the new fields.
risk_reasons: The public redeliver response drops `delivered`, which breaks clients

files.summary: Replaces the boolean `delivered` flag with a `DeliveryStatus` enum and adds an `attempts` counter. This is the vocabulary the rest of the PR uses.
look_for: Every reader of `delivered` is updated (see Impact)
Default values for existing persisted rows

notes.text: New `DeliveryStatus` enum. It subclasses `str`, so it serializes as `"delivered"` etc. in JSON responses.
Removing `delivered` breaks every reader of `delivery.delivered`, including `app/api/webhooks.py:13` and code outside this PR.

files.summary: New generic retry helper: `with_retry()` calls a function until it succeeds, sleeping with full-jitter exponential backoff between attempts.
look_for: Which exceptions are retried by default

notes.text: Full-jitter backoff: each delay is uniform in `[0, min(cap, base·2^n)]`, which spreads retries from many workers.
`retry_on` defaults to `Exception`, so programming errors (e.g. `KeyError`) are retried and slept on too.

files.summary: `send()` now wraps the POST in `with_retry()` and records the outcome in `status`/`attempts` instead of raising.
look_for: Which HTTP errors are retried (4xx vs 5xx)
Failures no longer raise — callers must check `status`
Total worst-case latency in the request path

notes.text: Each attempt increments `delivery.attempts` before the POST, so a delivery that fails 5 times reports `attempts == 5`.
`HTTPStatusError` covers 4xx too. A 404 or 400 is retried 5 times even though it can never succeed.

files.summary: The redeliver endpoint returns `status` and `attempts` instead of `delivered`, which is a **breaking change** to the public response.

notes.text: Response shape changes: `delivered` is removed. External consumers relying on it will break.

files.summary: Covers the happy path of `with_retry()` with `time.sleep` stubbed out.

notes.text: Only the success path is tested. Nothing covers exhausting retries, or `send()` marking a delivery `FAILED`.

chapters.title: Contracts: the new delivery state
chapters.goal: Start with the data model and the generic helper. Everything else builds on these.

files.why_now: Defines `DeliveryStatus`, the vocabulary the rest of the PR uses.
The retry helper has no webhook knowledge, so read it before its caller.

chapters.title: Behavior & API surface
chapters.goal: How sending uses the helper, how the API response changes, and what is tested.

files.why_now: Where retries actually happen; most of the risk is here.
Check what the tests cover against the risks you just saw.

flows.title: Redeliver request
flows.narrative: A redeliver request loads the delivery and calls `send()` (`app/delivery/sender.py:9`). `send()` hands an `attempt()` closure to `with_retry()` (`app/delivery/retry.py:14`), which POSTs to the customer endpoint and sleeps between failures using `backoff_delays()`. The final status is saved by the API handler.

impact.title: Redeliver API response drops `delivered`
impact.detail: Clients reading `response.delivered` get `undefined`/`KeyError`. Consider keeping it for one release.

impact.title: `WebhookDelivery.delivered` is read in 2 places outside this PR
impact.detail: These still read the removed attribute and will raise `AttributeError` at runtime.

impact.title: No data migration from `delivered` to `status`
impact.detail: Existing rows have `delivered = true` but will load as `status = PENDING`.

impact.title: Up to ~65s spent in the request thread
impact.detail: 5 attempts × 10s timeout plus backoff, all synchronous inside the redeliver handler.

impact.title: Retry exhaustion is untested
impact.detail: Add a test where every attempt fails.

questions.text: Should 4xx responses really be retried? A 404 can never succeed.
What is the migration plan for rows that already have `delivered = true`?

findings.title: Retrying on `HTTPStatusError` also retries 4xx responses, which will never succeed
findings.impact: Retrying on `HTTPStatusError` also retries 4xx responses, which will never succeed. Retry only on 5xx and 429?
findings.why: Retrying on `HTTPStatusError` also retries 4xx responses, which will never succeed. Retry only on 5xx and 429?
findings.comment_body: Retrying on `HTTPStatusError` also retries 4xx responses, which will never succeed. Retry only on 5xx and 429?

findings.title: `retry_on=(Exception,)` is very broad
findings.impact: `retry_on=(Exception,)` is very broad. Could callers opt in to specific exceptions instead?
findings.why: `retry_on=(Exception,)` is very broad. Could callers opt in to specific exceptions instead?
findings.comment_body: `retry_on=(Exception,)` is very broad. Could callers opt in to specific exceptions instead?

findings.title: This removes `delivered` from a public response
findings.impact:
This removes `delivered` from a public response. Can we keep it for one release?

```suggestion
    return {"id": result.id, "delivered": result.status == DeliveryStatus.DELIVERED, "status": result.status, "attempts": result.attempts}
```
findings.why:

findings.title: `RETRYING` is never set
findings.impact: `RETRYING` is never set. Drop it, or set it in `send()` between attempts.
